item.title: Advanced Observability with Amazon CloudWatch (CloudWatch Advanced Workshop)
item.description:
This hands-on lab on Advanced Observability with Amazon CloudWatch (CloudWatch Advanced Workshop) was conducted on Monday (26/10/2026) as part of Week 7. This document provides an exhaustive operational walkthrough covering automated infrastructure deployment via AWS CloudFormation, advanced metric calculations (Metric Math, Search Expressions, Dynamic Labels), log stream diagnostics using CloudWatch Logs Insights, log metric filters, multi-channel alerting with Amazon SNS, and operational dashboard creation.

🎯 Lab Objectives:

  • Automate the provisioning of a multi-instance compute fleet (Instance-A through Instance-E) using an AWS CloudFormation template (AwsWorkshopStack).
  • Master dynamic metric queries using Metric Math and automated Search Expressions (SEARCH('used', 'Average', 300) and SEARCH('disk_used_percent', 'Average')), allowing monitoring graphs to dynamically accommodate new instances without manual dashboard reconfiguration.
  • Standardize telemetry graph legends using Dynamic Labels ${PROP('Dim.DimName')} and ${PROP('Dim.InstanceId')} to enhance visual clarity and operational identification.
  • Connect securely to EC2 instances without opening inbound port 22 using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager (SSM), and execute a synthetic telemetry script (logger.py) pushing multi-level events to /var/log/messages.
  • Harness the full analytical capabilities of CloudWatch Logs Insights: write regex error filtering queries (like /ERROR/, like /WARN/), compute stream distribution aggregations (stats count(*) by @logStream), and render time-bucketed event histograms (stats count(*) by bin(5m)).
  • Extract quantifiable telemetry from unstructured log files using CloudWatch Metric Filters (PythonAppErrors), configure CloudWatch Alarms (PythonApplicationErrorAlarm1) integrated with Amazon SNS email notifications, and construct a centralized operations dashboard ssmDashboard.

item.title: Optimize Amazon EC2 Costs with AWS Lambda & Slack Notifications
item.description:
The Optimize Amazon EC2 Costs with AWS Lambda & Slack Notifications hands-on lab was conducted on Tuesday (20/10/2026) as part of Week 6. This document details the serverless operational automation architecture using AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge Scheduler, and ChatOps telemetry dispatching via Slack Incoming Webhooks.

🎯 Lab Objectives

  • Cloud Cost Optimization: Design and implement an automated compute scheduling architecture for Amazon EC2 instances, automatically stopping non-production development/test servers outside business hours and resuming them prior to the start of the workday, realizing up to 65 - 70% in compute cost savings.
  • Serverless Operational Automation: Develop serverless routines using AWS Lambda (Python 3 Boto3 SDK) coupled with Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to govern the complete compute lifecycle without maintaining any dedicated management host or cron server.
  • Dynamic Resource Tagging Governance: Apply tag-based identification strategies (environment_auto = true) enabling Lambda functions to dynamically query, filter, and control target instances without hardcoding instance IDs.
  • Real-Time ChatOps Telemetry via Slack: Integrate AWS Lambda with Slack channels using Incoming Webhooks, automatically broadcasting formatted operational alerts displaying instance transition states directly into the #notification channel.
  • Enterprise Troubleshooting Competence: Diagnose and resolve complex runtime exceptions, including state transition constraints (IncorrectInstanceState), ghost references to terminated instances, IAM policy evaluation boundaries, and resilient webhook dispatching.

item.title: Work with Amazon DynamoDB
item.description:
The Work with Amazon DynamoDB hands-on lab was conducted on Wednesday (14/10/2026) as part of Week 5. This document details the end-to-end implementation process across three operational methods: AWS Management Console, AWS CloudShell CLI, and Programmatic Automation with Python SDK (Boto3).
🔗 Workshop Source: Work with Amazon DynamoDB (Workshop 000060)

🎯 Lab Objectives:

  • Master the NoSQL architecture of Amazon DynamoDB, comprehend partition distribution mechanisms using Partition Key (HASH), composite key strategies using Composite Primary Key (HASH + RANGE), and schema flexibility with Scalar/Document attribute types.
  • Perform lifecycle management for the Music table via AWS Management Console: table creation, item insertion, in-place updates, conditional queries and full table scans, alongside configuring and querying a Global Secondary Index (GSI) named AlbumTitle-index.
  • Leverage the command-line interface of AWS CloudShell: authenticate via IAM credentials, provision tables, perform atomic CRUD operations (put-item, get-item, update-item, query), attach a GSI via update-table, and understand the asynchronous Backfilling phase.
  • Implement programmatic automation on Windows using Python 3 and Boto3 SDK: automated provisioning of the Movies table, item CRUD scripts, batch ingestion from a JSON payload (moviedata.json with 4,609 records), key-based queries, and filtered table scans (MoviesScan.py).
  • Analyze and document 10 in-depth real-world troubleshooting scenarios: workshop documentation flag typos, IAM policy authorization, duplicate resource conflicts, hidden zero-width Unicode characters (\u200b), terminal CLI pager behavior, GSI backfilling locks, environment execution mismatches, and multi-region routing.

  • Execute foundational network and security provisioning: verify VPC configuration, enable automatic public IPv4 addressing on the Public Subnet, and configure Security Groups allowing access to port 3000 (Grafana Web UI) and port 22 (SSH).
  • Configure the official Grafana RPM repository, install the software packages, and run the grafana-server background daemon managed by systemd on modern Amazon Linux 2023 (AL2023).

item.title: Deploy Amazon ElastiCache - Redis
item.description:
The Amazon ElastiCache - Redis workshop was conducted on Wednesday (10/14/2026) as part of Week 5. This document presents a comprehensive technical walkthrough: AWS Console configurations, infrastructure specifications, RBAC security hardening with Users and User Groups, programmatic automation with AWS CLI & Python Boto3 SDK, as well as hands-on troubleshooting of real-world operational challenges.
🔗 Reference Documentation: Amazon ElastiCache - Redis

🎯 Lab Objectives:

  • Design and provision an isolated VPC network topology with 3 Subnets distributed across 3 Availability Zones (us-east-1a, us-east-1b, us-east-1c) and configure an ElastiCache Subnet Group to satisfy Multi-AZ high availability and data sharding requirements.
  • Configure Security Group firewall policies permitting inbound traffic on TCP port 6379 (Redis) and TCP port 22 (SSH).
  • Provision an intermediate Amazon EC2 Client (redis-client) within the same VPC to interface with the private, isolated cache clusters.
  • Deploy and manage Redis clusters across both fundamental architectures:
    • Cluster Mode Disabled: 1 Shard, 1 Primary node, and 2 Replica nodes with automated failover (Auto-failover).
    • Cluster Mode Enabled: Multi-shard distributed architecture (3 Shards, 9 Nodes) enabling horizontal scaling and hash slot partitioning.
  • Fully automate Redis cluster provisioning utilizing the AWS CLI and the Python Boto3 SDK.
  • Implement enterprise-grade security controls: Transit Encryption (TLS) paired with Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) using custom Users and User Groups.
  • Develop Python client scripts to interact with Redis: cluster connectivity verification, string storage (Strings) with Time-to-Live (TTL), hash map data structures (Hash), and real-time asynchronous message streaming (Pub/Sub).
  • Resolve 12 critical technical challenges (Route Table Blackholes, missing package managers, deprecated third-party libraries, WRONGTYPE schema collisions, and User Group dependency errors).

    • Permissions options: Select Attach policies directly ➔ Attach AmazonElastiCacheFullAccess and AdministratorAccess to facilitate automated administration.

item.title: Monitoring with Amazon CloudWatch
item.description:
The Monitoring with Amazon CloudWatch hands-on lab was conducted on Thursday (08/10/2026) during Week 4. This page provides a comprehensive step-by-step implementation guide featuring precise configuration parameters, Logs Insights query syntax, Math Expressions, troubleshooting resolutions, and all 33 verification screenshots.
🔗 Lab Reference Material: Monitoring with Amazon CloudWatch

🎯 Lab Objectives:

  • Master the centralized monitoring and observability capabilities of Amazon CloudWatch on AWS.
  • Visualize and analyze real-time performance metrics (CloudWatch Metrics) across cloud infrastructure.
  • Utilize Search Expressions and Math Expressions to dynamically discover, aggregate, and normalize telemetry data.
  • Configure Dynamic Labels for context-aware and automated chart legends.
  • Ingest and analyze system logs (CloudWatch Logs) using the interactive query language CloudWatch Logs Insights.
  • Establish Metric Filters to extract actionable quantitative metrics from unstructured application log streams.
  • Configure CloudWatch Alarms integrated with Amazon SNS to automate proactive incident alerting.
